subject: SLA exception request: dedicated GPU pool throttle causing errors for Atlas Health
messages:
From: Sara Baines <sara@atlashealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: requests failing and latency high on production

Marissa/Vivek,

We're seeing a sharp increase in failed requests from our production traffic starting ~08:45 PDT. P95 latency has jumped from ~120ms to ~750ms and error_rate is ~4.7% (5xx + timeouts). This coincides with a "throttling" alert in your dashboard that mentions dedicated pool saturation. We're on a reserved capacity plan and have a committed throughput of 200 rps — our live telemetry shows sustained throughput at ~120 rps with retries.

This is impacting patient-facing flows; we need an ETA on mitigation and whether this will be covered under our SLA. Please escalate.

- Sara
Sara Baines
Sr. Product Manager
Atlas Health

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Immediate: requests failing and latency high on production

Marissa — initial findings below. Posting short summary, will follow with perf dumps.

Summary (initial):
- Root cause: dedicated GPU pool entered a degraded state due to an eviction/rebalancing race in our reserved-capacity allocator when a maintenance job compressed KV caches on a subset of nodes. That job temporarily reduced effective capacity (GPU memory pressure), causing requests to be queued and autoscaler to treat the pool as saturated.
- Observed impact: committed throughput 200 rps -> observed serving throughput ~120 rps; P95 latency rose to ~700–800ms; error spike (5xx/timeouts) ~4.5%.
- Why reserved capacity didn't shield them: our current allocator has a bug that prevents immediate fallback to burst nodes when pool reports degraded capacity under certain cache-eviction states.

Immediate mitigations we can take (order of preference):
1) Force-spin 3 warm dedicated nodes from the Dedicated pool in the customer's region (adds ~80–100 rps headroom). Can do in the next 12–15 minutes.
2) Temporarily route Atlas traffic to a compatible model variant on hosted capacity with burst allowance (requires live consent for data path change).
3) Cancel the maintenance job and reverse the KV compression; will restore capacity but takes ~30–40m to fully recover.

I'll produce perf_dump_20260602.json.gz and share logs; pushing a hotfix to allocator to unblock fallback will take ~3–6 hours (works on patch + rollout).

Connor O'Brien
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: perf_dump_20260602.json.gz

Sara — quick status and next steps from Redwood: 

What happened (short): our reserved-capacity allocator entered a degraded state during an internal maintenance job that compressed KV caches on some Dedicated nodes. The compression temporarily reduced available GPU memory on those nodes and our allocator misclassified the pool as saturated, preventing automatic fallback to burst nodes.

What we did (immediate):
- Force-spun 3 additional warm nodes into the Dedicated pool at 10:06 PDT; observed throughput climb from ~122 rps to ~190 rps within 9 minutes and P95 drop to ~160ms.
- Rolled back the maintenance job to prevent further evictions.
- Engineering is preparing a patch to the allocator that will be tested and rolled out (ETA 3–6 hours).

Compensation & SLA: Markus has approved issuing a pro-rated credit for the incident window. We will send the SLA exception form and a proposed credit amount by EOD for your review.

Next steps:
- Vivek will set up a 20-min call to review telemetry and confirm all systems green. Suggested times: 15:45 or 16:15 PDT. Please let us know which works.
- Follow-up post-mortem and remediation timeline (allocator patch) will be shared within 24 hours.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know this impacted your users and we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Marissa Cole
